modifications: Renamed from generate-cicd to oss-ci on migration into oss-kit.

Body split by forge. SKILL.md holds only the forge-independent process, which detects the ecosystem, decides what runs, chooses a matrix, and decides caching. All syntax moved out into references/github-actions.md and references/gitlab.md. Added a Scope section citing R-CI-01 through R-CI-05 from oss-kit's STANDARD.md, each with a two-word tag on one line.

references/best-practices.md renamed to references/github-actions.md and rewritten. Its Security section was removed, because that content belongs to oss-harden and the SEC rules, and the file now states its boundary with oss-harden and oss-publish outright. Concrete YAML for triggers, matrix, cache keying, timeout, and cancellation was added, so the file backs the R-CI rules it is cited against. It emits a version tag with a comment rather than a placeholder SHA, since pinning is R-SEC-01 and oss-harden's job. It also records that the secrets context does not parse inside a step's if:, and promotes the value into env: first.

references/gitlab.md is new in this fork, covering the same decisions in GitLab CI/CD syntax, with every keyword checked against the current GitLab CI/CD YAML reference before it was written. Recorded there: cache .npm/ with npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline rather than a node_modules cache that npm ci empties; workflow:auto_cancel:on_new_commit and workflow:rules:auto_cancel are the path to auto-cancellation; cache:key:files takes at most two files and expands no variable; sast is available on GitLab Free with its advanced features gated to Ultimate; and the closest equivalent to a GitHub Actions uses: step is a CI/CD component.

Both reference files carry a static-site deployment section, GitHub Pages and GitLab Pages, checked against each vendor's documentation on 2026-07-27. It cites no rule ID, because no rule in STANDARD.md requires a project to publish a site, and Step 3 asks before writing one. Recorded there: GitHub documents pages: write and id-token: write on the deploying job, while its own starter workflow grants both at the top level and so violates R-SEC-02; a Pages deployment inverts R-CI-05's cancellation guidance on both forges; and GitHub ignores a CNAME file entirely when publishing from a custom Actions workflow, which makes a custom domain a settings-only change.

Cache policy prefers official setup-action caching, hashes lockfiles, separates compatibility boundaries, and treats stale fallback restoration as optional, because GitHub defines restore-keys as prefixes for stale caches. Matrix coverage follows every supported release line, applicable project checks replace a mandatory lint-test-build trio, and GitLab does not cancel diagnostic jobs on the first failure.

The fork owns R-CI-06 and cites it in Step 2 and in the Scope section, so a repository that ships executable code and defines no automated test suite is a gap this skill raises rather than a class of check the project does without. Upstream generate-cicd presumes a suite already exists and writes only the pipeline around it.

The Scope section's ban on writing a permissions: block carries one exception, the two blocks the GitHub Pages section emits, because a Pages deploy authenticates through them and a workflow written without them cannot run. The GitHub Pages workflow is two jobs rather than one, so the privileged token never shares a job with the project's build command, and both forges' Pages blocks mark which lines are copied exactly and which are placeholders. Recorded there: actions/configure-pages belongs in the build job before the build command, because exporting the base path afterwards leaves a green run serving a site whose asset paths resolve against the domain root. Each policy is stated once, in SKILL.md, and each reference file carries only the syntax that expresses it, so the R-CI-02 and R-CI-03 restatements the two files carried are gone. Step 6 tells the reader to open one reference file and not the other and carries the fail-fast ordering sentence for both forges, Step 5 states the cache preference in forge-neutral terms, and Step 7 records that the forge CLI need not be installed to print the command that adds a secret. The skill names two ways in, and one of them reviews an existing workflow or pipeline against each R-CI Check line and changes no file; upstream generates configuration only. references/gitlab.md carries a CI/CD variables section with no upstream counterpart, checked against GitLab's own CI/CD variables and merge request pipelines documentation and the glab command reference on 2026-07-30: glab variable set defaults to an unmasked, unprotected variable, GitLab masks only a single-line value of 8 characters or more with no spaces, and a merge request pipeline reaches a protected variable only when both branches are protected and belong to the same project, never from a fork.

references/ecosystems/ holds one file per ecosystem in oss-kit's roster: npm, PyPI, RubyGems, crates.io, Go modules, Packagist, NuGet, Maven Central, Hex, pub.dev, and container images. Each carries the same three sections, the setup action or image per forge and where the manifest states the supported versions (R-CI-03), the package manager's cache directory and the file that keys it (R-CI-04), and the canonical test invocation and where the project declares it (R-CI-06), and each states what it read and when. Step 2 routes to them from a table of manifest signals, on what the repository has rather than what it publishes, because a manifest that exists only for development still gets installed in CI. Upstream generate-cicd carries no per-ecosystem facts at all. Recorded there and checked upstream on 2026-07-31: actions/setup-go keys its cache on go.mod by default rather than go.sum; actions/setup-dotnet's cache input fails outright when no packages.lock.json exists, and NuGet lock files are opt-in; actions/setup-java hashes pom.xml for Maven because Apache Maven publishes no lockfile, and its Gradle hash list does not match gradle.lockfile; ruby/setup-ruby caches installed gems under vendor/bundle by design and generates a lockfile with bundle lock when the repository commits none; erlef/setup-beam and dart-lang/setup-dart offer no cache input at all, and Hex documents no cache directory, so both files carry a stated gap rather than a recipe; a Dart library commits no pubspec.lock, so it has no lockfile to key on; neither the PHP project nor Composer publishes a setup action; and the Rust project publishes none either, so the Cargo book's own CI chapter drives rustup directly. The npm-specific YAML in the two forge references stays where it is, as worked syntax examples rather than a claim about ecosystem coverage.
